The misconception we've given you — that science can explain away miracles — is a very real reality in the life of our students. They're taught that, and they're conditioned to believe it. They're conditioned for that to be the default. Instead of thinking right away that something might be a miracle, they're conditioned to think right away that something can just be explained by science.

paragraphs.heading: When miracles get personal
paragraphs.edited: One thing to keep in mind as you're navigating through this: although we talk a lot about the fact that miracles are possible and verifiable and that they do happen, and we see throughout Scripture that God works in mighty ways, and we want to boast that miracles happen all throughout the world, this can also be a very, very personal thing. Miracles can bring up really, really important questions in the lives of our students.

But this can also be a very, very personal thing. Miracles can bring up really, really important questions in the lives of our students.
